diveTitle: What actually happens when you convert
diveSubtitle: The details that matter once you go beyond the basics.
dive1Title: Why convert away from WebP at all?
dive1Desc: WebP is efficient but not universally supported — some older software, certain email clients, and specific upload forms still don't recognize it. Converting to PNG trades some file size for guaranteed compatibility with virtually anything that opens image files.
dive2Desc: PNG supports transparency just as fully as WebP does, so any transparent areas in your source image convert perfectly with no loss — nothing gets filled in or flattened during this conversion.
dive3Title: If your WebP was compressed with quality loss
dive3Desc: If the original WebP was saved using lossy compression, that quality loss already happened and can't be undone by converting to PNG — you'll get a PNG that faithfully preserves whatever quality the WebP had, not a restored original.
dive4Title: Expect the file to get bigger
dive4Desc: PNG is generally larger than WebP for the same image, since WebP's compression is more efficient. This is a normal trade-off when converting for compatibility rather than file size — don't be surprised if the PNG is noticeably heavier.
dive5Desc: This tool converts static images. An animated WebP converts using only its first frame, since PNG doesn't support the same multi-frame animation format — for animated content, you'd need a GIF or video export instead.
dive6Title: When you actually need PNG instead of WebP
dive6Desc: Common reasons: an upload form or CMS that rejects WebP files, older editing software, or printing workflows that expect standard formats. If none of those apply and file size matters, it's often worth keeping the WebP instead of converting.
faqTitle: Questions We Get All the Time
faq1Q: Is this WEBP to PNG converter really free?
faq1A: Yes — you can use it for free, without creating an account and without watermarks. The free plan allows 5 uses per day and has a file-size limit; paid plans raise them.
faq2Q: Will the PNG quality be as good as the original WEBP?
faq2A: Actually, PNG can look even sharper than WEBP in some cases because it uses lossless compression. You won't lose any pixel data during the conversion — what you see in the preview is exactly what you get.
faq3Q: Why would I convert WEBP to PNG?
faq3A: WEBP is great for web performance, but it's not universally supported. Older software, some design tools, and most print workflows expect PNG or JPG. Converting to PNG gives you the widest compatibility without sacrificing image quality.
faq4Q: How long are my files kept on the server?
faq4A: Your uploaded files and converted PNGs are automatically deleted within 1 hour. Once you close the download page, they're gone — we don't keep copies.
faq5Q: Can I convert WEBP files with transparency to PNG?
faq5A: Absolutely. PNG supports full alpha transparency, so any transparent areas in your WEBP will be faithfully preserved in the output. This makes it ideal for logos, icons, and design assets.
seo1Title: WEBP vs PNG — Which Should You Use?
seo1P1: Google introduced the WEBP format back in 2010 to make the web faster. At the same size, a WEBP image typically looks better than a JPEG and loads quicker than a PNG. That's why you'll find WEBP everywhere on modern websites — it's the format browsers love.
seo1P2: The problem is that WEBP doesn't travel well. Try opening a WEBP in Photoshop (without a plugin), email it to a client, or drop it into a Word document — and you'll quickly run into issues. PNG is the universal format that works everywhere: design software, presentations, print shops, messaging apps. When you need your image to just work, PNG is the safe choice.
seo2Title: When You Actually Need to Convert WEBP to PNG

Social media platforms, stock image sites, and website builders all export in WEBP now — but downstream tools haven't caught up. Our converter handles that gap quietly and quickly.
